name: UV photoprocessing and FTIR transmission/RAIRS spectroscopy of interstellar ice analogues deposited at 14 K on KBr in a UHV closed-cycle helium cryostat (INFRA-ICE, 1e-10 mbar)
plain_name: Make space-like ice at 14 K in ultra-high vacuum and watch it change under UV light
description: INFRA-ICE (ICMM-CSIC Stardust machine): ices (CH4, undecane) are background-deposited at 14 K on IR-transparent KBr substrates held in a 9 mm aperture holder on a UHV closed-cycle helium cryostat (13-300 K, 0.1 K stability) at a base pressure of 1e-10 mbar (5e-11 mbar cold), irradiated with a windowless UV discharge lamp and measured by FTIR through wedged ZnSe windows.
keywords: Make space-like ice at 14 K in ultra-high vacuum and watch it change under UV light

sources.citation: G. Santoro, J. M. Sobrado, G. Tajuelo-Castilla et al., 'INFRA-ICE: an ultra-high vacuum experimental station for laboratory astrochemistry', Rev. Sci. Instrum. 91, 124101 (2020), doi:10.1063/5.0027920 (PMC7116743)

reported_equipment: INFRA-ICE UHV module of the Stardust machine (ICMM-CSIC)

requirements.rationale: Ices are deposited and processed at 14 K to simulate dark-cloud grain mantles.
The ice must be grown and processed in UHV to avoid contamination by residual gas.
UHV base pressure of 1e-10 mbar keeps background water accretion negligible during long irradiations.
FTIR transmission and reflection-absorption spectra are recorded through IR windows (wedged ZnSe) into the UHV chamber.
Optional: the KBr substrate sits behind a 9 mm diameter aperture in the sample holder.
Optional: the cryostat regulates the sample with 0.1 K stability.
Optional: cooling is by a UHV closed-cycle helium cryostat.

confirmation_note: Requirements taken from the cited procedure and independently re-verified against the source (research/v4, 2026-11-01). Users must confirm them for their own run; edits require confirmation again.
